name: Neapolitan
description: The Naples original: soft, blistered cornicione from a 900F wood oven in about 90 seconds. Where to eat real Neapolitan pizza, ranked by taste.

name: Neapolitan Contemporanea
description: Modern Naples pizza: long-fermented, high-hydration dough with a tall, airy cornicione. Where to eat pizza contemporanea, ranked by taste.

name: Italian Style
description: The everyday Italian round pie, thin and pliable in the center with a blistered rim. Where to eat classic Italian pizza, ranked by taste.

name: Roman-Style
description: Pizza tonda romana, rolled thin and baked cracker-crisp edge to edge in a hot oven. Where to eat Roman-style pizza, ranked by taste.

name: Pizza al Taglio
description: Roman pizza baked in trays and sold by weight: high-hydration dough, long ferment, crisp base. Where to eat pizza al taglio, ranked.

name: Pinsa
description: Roman pinsa: an oval, airy flatbread from a wheat, rice and soy blend, long-fermented and crisp. Where to eat pinsa, ranked.

name: Pizza Fritta
description: Naples street pizza fried, not baked: the dough folded or stuffed and blistered in hot oil. Where to eat pizza fritta, ranked by taste.

name: New York-Style
description: Wide, thin, foldable slices from a hot gas deck oven, built on high-gluten dough. Where to eat New York-style pizza, ranked by taste.

name: New Haven Apizza
description: New Haven's coal-fired pies: thin, oblong, charred, and known for the white clam pie. Where to eat apizza, ranked by taste.

name: Pizza alla Pala
description: Roman pizza shaped long on a wooden peel, baked on the stone: high-hydration dough, light and crisp, sold by the length.

name: Detroit-Style
description: Thick, airy squares baked in steel pans with cheese caramelized to a crust at the edges. Where to eat Detroit-style pizza, ranked.

name: Chicago Deep-Dish
description: A deep, buttery crust layered cheese-first with sauce on top, baked long and cut thick. Where to eat Chicago deep-dish, ranked.

name: Sicilian
description: Thick, airy rectangular pizza with roots in Palermo's sfincione, baked in an oiled pan. Where to eat Sicilian-style pizza, ranked.

name: Pizza al Padellino
description: Turin's small round pan pizza: thick, soft, and light with a fried-crisp base. Where to eat pizza al padellino, ranked by taste.

name: Argentine
description: Buenos Aires made pizza its own: thick media masa piled with muzzarella, onion-stuffed fugazzeta, and chickpea fainá stacked on the slice.
